analysis.title: GS Blekos - Marketcolour + Earnings Snippets ECB 30 Oct 2026
key_insights: US equities finished Thursday mixed: SPX -30 bps to 7720, NDX -138 bps to 28,402, RTY +101 bps to 2859. 8 of 11 sectors finished higher.
Equal-weight S&P (SPW) outperformed SPX by 150 bps, the third-largest single-day move YTD. Healthcare +2.50%, Real Estate +2.25%, Communication Services -6.60%.
Consumer names caught a bid on rotation out of tech. The GS Discretionary basket (GSXUCOND) finished +3.29%.
Mega-cap tech fell on disappointing earnings. GOOG, NOW and FTNT fell 10-15% in NDX. Post-bell, AMZN fell 5% and NOW dropped 26.96% after a weak Q3 report.
AMZN's post-bell drop is its worst single-day return in its listed history at about -12%, a 6.5-sigma move, per the desk.
Over 60% of SPX members are down 20% from their local highs. Four of the Mag7 are in bear market territory, erasing about USD 4trn of market cap.
Europe closed higher for a fourth straight session: SXXP +80 bps, SX5E +60 bps. Defense (GSSBDEFE +3.6%, KOG NO +13%), Software (GSSBSFTW +1.1%) and Semis (GSSBSEMI +2%) stood out.

Flow: Asset managers were slight net sellers (supply in communication services and discretionary, demand in macro). Hedge fund flows were roughly flat. Single-stock activity did not rise materially despite the size of the moves. Trading was top-down, with SPX volume 35% above the 20-day average.
AMZN: AWS growth of 39% in the quarter was below expectations. Management guided in the press release to AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028.

INTC fell 17%. 3Q data center and AI revenue rose 78% y/y, but 4Q revenue guidance of $15-16bn is well below consensus of $17.29bn. Management expects the PC slowdown to continue at least through H1 of next year.
PINS fell 16%. 3Q revenue of $1.17bn missed consensus of $1.2bn, and 4Q revenue and EBITDA guidance is below the Street.

SNDK was unchanged. Gross margin was 85% in the quarter, revenue beat, EPS was nearly $50 per share, an 8:1 stock split was announced, and about $5bn of stock was bought back. 4Q revenue guidance is in line with the Street.

ECB: GS keeps its forecast of one more hike in December. Sovereign stress could lead the Council to hold, but the tightening in financial conditions needed would likely have to be large given energy pressures. A March hike is possible if energy prices keep rising. GS sees a significant hurdle to faster hikes.
AMZN rated Buy with PT cut to USD 370 from USD 375, 50% upside. Thesis rests on AWS Gen AI workloads, e-commerce margin gains from logistics efficiency, and high-margin advertising growth.
Europe earnings: CAP beat and raised, UMG better than feared, Alpha Bank strong beat, CaixaBank negative feedback, SCOR 3Q net income about 17% above company-collected consensus, AXA GWP in line.
CTA model has CTAs short SX5E, which would need to be bought back at current levels (medium-term threshold 6182, short-term threshold 6238).

earnings_insights: AMZN (reported 10/29 post-bell): AWS growth 39% in the quarter, below expectations. Management guides to AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028. Stock -10% (after -4% today) per the desk.
INTC (reported): 3Q data center and AI revenue +78% y/y. 4Q revenue guidance $15-16bn vs consensus $17.29bn. Management expects the PC slowdown to continue at least through H1 of next year.
PINS (reported): 3Q revenue $1.17bn vs consensus $1.2bn. 4Q revenue and EBITDA guidance below the Street.
SNDK (reported): gross margin 85% in the quarter, revenue beat, EPS nearly $50 per share, 8:1 stock split, about $5bn repurchased in the quarter, 4Q revenue guidance in line with the Street.

CAP (reported 3Q): organic growth 5.2% vs sell-side 3.9%. FY organic growth guide raised to 4-4.5% from 3.5-4% (street 4.1%). Operating margin guide 13.6% to 13.8% unchanged. Organic free cash flow guide about EUR 1.8-1.9bn unchanged. Book-to-bill 89% vs a seasonal norm of 95-96%.
UMG (reported 3Q): streaming subscription growth ex-downtown 9.5% vs street about 8.5% and bears at 6-7%. Margin 21.5%, 90 bps above the Street.

Alpha Bank (reported 3Q): net profit beat by 15%, driven by a 6% NII beat, 2% fees beat, 3% lower expenses and lower loan loss provisions. Loans and deposits both up 13% y/y. CET1 20 bps better. GS expects the stock up 3-5%.
CaixaBank (reported 3Q): negative feedback. NII up 5% y/y in Q3 vs consensus of +13% y/y for FY2027, so volume and NII trends are likely to pressure next year's earnings.

SCOR (reported 3Q26): net income about 17% above company-collected consensus, including a P&C Re insurance service result beat of about 10% and an L&H Re beat of 5%. Normalised combined ratio about 81%.

AXA (reported 3Q26): GWP broadly in line with company-collected consensus (+1%). P&C and Health beat by 3%, offset by lower life premiums. P&C commercial lines GWP +1% y/y comparable vs GS expectation of roughly flat.

macro_indicators.reading: One more hike expected at the December meeting; March hike possible
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS expects the ECB to keep tightening despite sovereign stress and energy pressures. A faster pace of hikes is unlikely.

tension_points.bear_case: AWS grew 39%, below expectations, and AMZN, NOW, GOOG, INTC and PINS fell on weak results or guidance. Over 60% of SPX members are down 20% from highs and four Mag7 names are in bear markets.

tension_points.what_invalidates: A large tightening in financial conditions from sovereign stress would be needed to lead the Council to hold in December.
